name: Website Design & Development
tagline: A site that does the selling for you.
summary: Hand-built websites and web apps: hotels, restaurants, schools, hospitals, organisations and brands. Every one of the sites below is deployed and live — open any of them on the phone in your hand and judge the thing itself.
forWhom: A business that is losing customers to a website it is embarrassed to send. A school, hotel, hospital, restaurant, church or founder who needs one place that answers the question and takes the booking.
problem: A slow template costs money quietly. The visitor who cannot load you in three seconds becomes somebody else's customer, and you never hear about it. The fix is not a prettier template — it is a site built around the one action you need a visitor to take.
approach: We start with the action: a booking, an order, an enquiry, a registration. Everything on the page serves it.
Built on the same stack this site runs on, so pages open fast on a mid-range phone and a thin connection.
Written to be read on a phone held in one hand, with the phone number and the next step always in reach.
You get the deployment, the domain under your name and a walkthrough. Nothing is held hostage.
outcomes: A booking, order or enquiry path that works end to end
Pages that open in under a second on 4G
Search-ready structure and metadata from day one
A site you can send to a customer without apologising

process.d: We open your current site on a phone, on a slow connection, and write down what it costs you.
Booking, order, call, register. One job per page, decided before a pixel is drawn.
Design in the browser, built by hand, reviewed on a real phone at every step.
Deploy, connect your domain, set up analytics, and walk your team through editing it.

faqs.q: How long does a site take?
faqs.a: A single-page site is days. A full hotel, school or hospital site with booking and content is a few weeks. You get a date before we start.
Yes. Content lives in structured files your team can edit, and we walk you through it at handover.

faqs.q: Can I buy one of the finished sites on this page?
faqs.a: Yes. The sites marked For sale are complete builds we own. You buy it, we put your name, your photos and your prices on it, and it goes live on your domain.

name: Brand & Graphic Design
tagline: Design that gets stopped in the scroll.
summary: Flyers, campaign artwork, product design and identity work — made in association with Motionverse, the design partner that co-founded KR8 Digitals. The work below is client work, published with permission.
forWhom: Businesses running campaigns on WhatsApp and Instagram, product brands launching a range, schools and events that need artwork people actually stop for.
problem: A flyer is not decoration. It is the first and often only impression a customer gets of you, seen for half a second on a phone between two other posts. Most small-business artwork loses that half second.
approach: One message per piece. If everything is loud, nothing is heard.
Designed at the size it will be seen: a phone screen, not a print proof.
Product, price and contact placed where the eye already goes.
Delivered in the formats the platforms actually want, plus a template for reuse.
outcomes: Artwork that holds attention in a crowded feed
A consistent look across campaigns and platforms
Print and screen files, correctly sized
Reusable templates for your team to run without us

process.d: What is being sold, to whom, and what has to happen when they see it.
One route, shown with real copy, not latin.
Artwork built at phone size first, then adapted outward.
Every size and format you need, plus the editable file.

faqs.a: Motionverse is a co-founder of KR8 Digitals. Design work is made in association with Motionverse, and we credit it because it is true.

faqs.q: Is the work on this page really yours?
faqs.a: Yes. Every flyer below was designed for the client named on it. Open one at full size and read the artwork.

faqs.q: Can you work from my existing brand?
faqs.a: Yes — we build on what you have, or we rebuild the identity if it is working against you.

name: Video Editing & Production
tagline: Cut for the way people actually watch.
summary: Vertical-first editing for testimonials, product films and social cuts: captions, pacing, sound and a poster frame that earns the tap. The films below are real cuts, playing on this page.
forWhom: Anyone with footage sitting unused — a phone full of testimonials, an event nobody edited, a product that needs to be seen moving.
problem: Footage is not a film. An unedited testimonial is a favour to nobody: no captions, no pace, no reason to keep watching past second three. The edit is the difference between proof and noise.
approach: Cut for sound-off viewing first: captions burned in, story legible without audio.
Vertical by default, horizontal when the venue needs it.
Trim to the moment that proves the point, then stop.
Deliver a poster frame so the first thing a viewer sees is a face, not a black rectangle.
outcomes: Testimonials that are actually watchable to the end
Captions and safe-area framing for social
Poster frames and file sizes that load on mobile data
A library you can keep posting from

process.d: All of it. We mark the twenty seconds that matter.
Hook, proof, close — in that order, at phone length.
Pace, sound, and captions that survive being watched on mute.
Every aspect ratio and length the platforms want, plus posters.

faqs.a: We can direct a shoot. Most of the work here started as phone footage that needed a proper edit — that is the cheaper route and often the better one.

faqs.q: Whose videos are on this page?
faqs.a: Real cuts from our own school and client work. They play in place — press one.

name: SEO Optimisation
tagline: Be the answer when someone searches.
summary: Technical work, content structure and local visibility so the people already looking for what you do can find you. No promises about positions; a clear record of what was fixed and what moved.
forWhom: A business that exists but cannot be found. A site that is invisible on a phone search. An organisation whose name gets misspelled into somebody else's result.
problem: Search rewards structure, not adjectives. Most sites are missing the basics — titles, descriptions, structured data, a sitemap, a page for each thing they sell — and no amount of keyword stuffing fixes a page Google cannot parse.
approach: Fix the technical floor first: titles, metadata, structured data, sitemap, speed, mobile.
Give every service and every location a page of its own instead of one crowded home page.
Write for the question the customer types, not the award you want to win.
Report monthly on what changed — ranks are the outcome, not the method.
outcomes: Every page with a real title and description
Structured data so search and social show the right thing
A sitemap that is submitted and read
A monthly record of what was done and what moved

process.d: Crawl the site. List what search cannot read.
Metadata, schema, sitemap, speed, mobile rendering.
A page per service, per programme, per place.
What we did, what the numbers did, what is next.

faqs.a: Nobody honest gives you a date. Technical fixes can show within weeks; content takes months. We report against what we changed.
No. Anyone who does is selling you something else.

faqs.q: Can you fix a site you did not build?
faqs.a: Yes. That is most of the work.

name: AI & Automation
tagline: Take the repetitive work off a human.
summary: Forms that route themselves, assistants that answer the questions your team answers forty times a day, and systems that write the follow-up nobody has time to write. Working examples are on this page — including the assistant on this site.
forWhom: A team drowning in the same five questions. A business losing enquiries in an inbox nobody owns. Anyone paying a person to copy data between two screens.
problem: Most 'AI projects' are a demo that never ships. The useful ones are small, unglamorous and measurable: a form that reaches the right desk, an answer given at 2am, a follow-up that goes out on time.
approach: Find the task that repeats, not the task that impresses.
Ship the smallest version that removes the work, then measure it.
Keep a human in the loop for anything that promises or prices.
Log every conversation so nothing disappears into a black box.
outcomes: Enquiries routed to the right person automatically
Answers available outside working hours
Fewer dropped leads, with a record of every one
A system your team can actually maintain

process.d: Where does a message go, who answers it, what gets missed.
The smallest system that changes that path.
The awkward ones: typos, mixed languages, half a question.
You own the prompts, the logic and the logs.

faqs.a: Routing, first replies, follow-ups, data entry, scheduling, reminders, summaries and search over your own documents. Tell us the task that repeats most and we will tell you honestly whether it is worth automating.
Two. The assistant on this site answers questions and hands off to a human, and the Jev form router decides whether a message is a lead, a contact request or an issue.
It replaces the part of the job nobody wanted: the fortieth copy-paste of the day.
